error_message: stitch MCP: 'Failed to connect - Incompatible auth server: does not support dynamic client registration'
root_cause: stitch was configured as an http server at https://stitch.googleapis.com/mcp. That endpoint requires a pre-registered OAuth client; Claude Code only performs dynamic client registration, so authentication can never succeed. Re-running the OAuth flow cannot fix it.
fix: Replaced with the stdio proxy: claude mcp add stitch -s user -e STITCH_API_KEY=<key> -- npx -y @_davideast/stitch-mcp proxy. The proxy hard-errors without STITCH_API_KEY or STITCH_ACCESS_TOKEN.

error_message: mcp__stitch__download_assets returned 'Assets downloaded to <dir>' but wrote no files anywhere on disk
root_cause: download_assets is a proxy-side convenience tool in @_davideast/stitch-mcp, not a real Stitch API call. It reports success unconditionally and silently writes nothing. Verified by searching the whole filesystem for files modified in the last 15 minutes.
fix: Ignore the tool. Take htmlCode.downloadUrl / screenshot.downloadUrl from list_screens and curl them. The html download URL is a base64 protobuf in which only the html_<32hex> file id varies, so every screen's URL is reconstructable from a constant prefix+suffix; the URLs need no auth.

error_message: e: Cannot access 'androidx.room3.RoomDatabase' which is a supertype of 'AnfasDatabase'. Check your module classpath for missing or conflicting dependencies.
root_cause: :core:database declared `implementation(libs.bundles.room)`, but AnfasDatabase extends RoomDatabase and DatabaseBuilderFactory returns RoomDatabase.Builder — room3-runtime is part of the module's ABI, so a consumer (:core:data) could not compile against it.
fix: Split the bundle: `api(libs.androidx.room3.runtime)` because it is in the ABI, `implementation(libs.androidx.sqlite.bundled)` because the driver is internal to buildDatabase(). Features still never see Room — anfas.kmp.feature withholds :core:database.

error_message: e: Name contains illegal characters: ",". (core/data + feature/members commonTest, only on compileTestKotlinIosSimulatorArm64)
root_cause: Backtick-quoted test function names containing a comma. The JVM target accepts them, so `:core:data:jvmTest` passed and the failure only appeared when `check` reached the Kotlin/Native test compilation.
fix: Stripped , ; : . from all backticked test names. Lesson: run `./gradlew check` (which compiles native test targets) before believing a KMP test suite is green — a jvmTest pass proves nothing about iOS.

error_message: e: Unresolved reference 'number' (kotlinx.datetime.Month.number)
root_cause: kotlinx-datetime 0.8.0's Month has no `number` property.
fix: Index a MonthAbbreviations array by Enum.ordinal; the enum is declared January..December in order.

error_message: e: Overload resolution ambiguity / Conflicting overloads in OfflineFirstMemberRepository.kt (runStorage, asStorageError)
root_cause: Extracted the shared error-boundary helpers into StorageBoundary.kt as `internal` while OfflineFirstMemberRepository.kt still had its own `private` copies with the same names in the same package.
fix: Deleted the private copies and rewrote the member repository to use the shared runStorage/asAppResult. Extracting a helper means removing the original, not adding a second.

error_message: e: Cannot access class 'kotlinx.datetime.LocalDate'. Check your module classpath (from :core:data)
root_cause: kotlinx-datetime was `implementation` in :core:model, but SubscriptionTerm.startsOn and RenewalQuote.endsOn expose LocalDate, so it is part of the module's ABI. Same class of mistake as bug-003 with room3.
fix: Changed to `api(libs.kotlinx.datetime)`. Rule: if a type from a dependency appears in your public signatures, it is `api`.

error_message: e: Unresolved reference 'datetime' in core/common/RelativeTime.kt — only during :core:common:compileCommonMainKotlinMetadata
root_cause: kotlinx-datetime was reached transitively via api(project(":core:model")). Platform compilations (jvmTest) resolved it, but commonMain *metadata* compilation did not, so `:core:common:jvmTest` passed while `check` failed later.
fix: Declared api(libs.kotlinx.datetime) directly in :core:common. Do not rely on a transitive api dependency in commonMain metadata compilation; declare ABI deps explicitly.

error_message: app.cash.turbine.TurbineAssertionError: Unconsumed events found (3 ReminderQueueComponentTest failures)
root_cause: A StateFlow keeps emitting after the assertion of interest — combine() re-emits when any upstream changes. Turbine treats leftover emissions at the end of a test() block as a failure.
fix: End each state.test { } block with cancelAndIgnoreRemainingEvents() once the interesting emission has been asserted.

error_message: e: Unresolved reference. None of the following candidates is applicable because of a receiver type mismatch (clock.now().todayIn(zone))
root_cause: kotlinx-datetime's todayIn is an extension on Clock, not on Instant.
fix: Call clock.todayIn(timeZone) directly.

error_message: AssertionError: expected:<[#88393, #88394]> but was:<[#88394]> — only one member imported instead of two
root_cause: The test fixture's newId lambda returned a constant string, so every imported row got the same member primary key and the Room upsert collapsed them into a single row. The repository was correct; the double-checked assertion caught the fixture.
fix: Made the fixture's newId a counter. Lesson: any injected id generator in a test must be unique per call, or upserts silently merge records and the test looks like a product bug.

error_message: e: Conflicting import: imported name 'IntakeReviewComponent' is ambiguous (RootComponent.kt)
root_cause: A python str.replace patch inserted the same import block twice because the anchor line appeared more than once in the file after an earlier partial edit.
fix: Deduplicated the imports by hand. When patching source with replace(), pass a count or assert the anchor occurs exactly once first.

root_cause: 2 lines replaced/restructured
fix: Rewrote 3→42 lines (2 removed)

root_cause: Code path had no error handling — exceptions would propagate uncaught
fix: Added try/catch block

error_message: Error resolving plugin [id: 'org.jetbrains.kotlin.plugin.serialization', version: '2.4.10'] > already on the classpath with an unknown version
root_cause: Applied the anfas.quality convention plugin at the ROOT project. That puts the convention project's entire runtime classpath -- including the Kotlin plugins -- on the root buildscript classpath, which every subproject inherits. Subprojects then cannot resolve their own plugin versions.
fix: Root applies Spotless by version-catalog alias instead, with its own small spotless block for root-level .kts. Modules get formatting via their anfas.* convention plugin. Never apply a convention plugin to the root project of this build.

error_message: Execution failed for task ':feature:announcements:spotlessKotlin' > Could not read path '.../merged_res/androidHostTest/.../values-ne_values-ne.arsc.flat'
root_cause: Spotless had targetExclude("**/build/**"), which forces it to ENUMERATE build intermediates in order to exclude them. AGP deletes merged-resource files mid-build, so the enumeration hit a file that had vanished.
fix: Dropped the targetExclude entirely. target("src/**/*.kt") already cannot match build/, which is a sibling of src/. Scope targets narrowly instead of excluding broadly.

error_message: Configuration cache problems: Task ':verifyIosVersionConfig' cannot serialize Gradle script object references
root_cause: A doLast block referenced a script-level function (renderIosVersionConfig). Task actions are serialized for the configuration cache and cannot capture script objects.
fix: Render the expected text at CONFIGURATION time into a local String and have the task action capture only that. Also: do not declare a generated file as an input of the task that verifies it -- Gradle reports an implicit task dependency. Use outputs.upToDateWhen { false } for a verification task instead.

error_message: androidx.sqlite.SQLiteException: Error code: 1555, UNIQUE constraint failed: room_master_table.id (MigrationV4ToV5Test)
root_cause: The test hand-inserted the schema identity hash into room_master_table, but a Room schema JSON's setupQueries ALREADY contain both the CREATE TABLE and the INSERT OR REPLACE for that row.
fix: Execute the schema's setupQueries verbatim and add no manual insert. Room will not recognise a hand-built database as being at version N without that row, so it must come from exactly one place.

error_message: macOS has no `timeout` command -- a verification run silently never started ('command not found: timeout')
root_cause: Used `timeout 90 ./gradlew ...` to bound a run. GNU coreutils is not present on macOS by default, so the whole pipeline failed and the absence of the expected log file was misread as a code problem.
fix: Background the process and poll for the expected condition with an until-loop, then pkill. Do not assume GNU coreutils on this machine.

error_message: expected:<[01001234567]> but was:<[٠١٠٠١٢٣٤٥٦٧]> -- duplicate phone detection silently failing
root_cause: Char.isDigit() returns TRUE for Arabic-Indic digits (U+0660..U+0669), so filter { it.isDigit() } kept them and the same phone number in Arabic numerals produced a different normalisation key. All 18 existing tests used Latin digits.
fix: Fold Arabic-Indic and Eastern Arabic digits to ASCII BEFORE filtering (TextNormalisation.foldDigitsToAscii). Rule: never use isDigit() as a filter when non-Latin input is possible -- fold first.

error_message: Compose MP 1.11.1 has no public API to override the Resources locale; iOS locale changes need an app relaunch
root_cause: LocalComposeEnvironment is internal and ResourceEnvironment has an internal constructor. On iOS, Locale.current reads NSLocale.preferredLanguages, changeable only via NSUserDefaults AppleLanguages and effective next launch.
fix: Do not use Compose Resources for strings when an in-app language toggle is required. A typed AppStrings interface behind a CompositionLocal makes switching an ordinary recomposition on all platforms, and makes a missing translation a compile error.

error_message: Overlay boxes would jump to mirrored positions over a photograph in Arabic
root_cause: Modifier.offset IS layout-direction aware (it negates x under RTL); absoluteOffset is the direction-agnostic one. The plan initially had this backwards. A photograph is not a mirrored artifact, so mirroring the overlay points staff at the wrong line.
fix: Force LocalLayoutDirection = Ltr on the entire image pane, not absoluteOffset on one call -- that also covers future Alignment/Arrangement/gesture code. Fixed alongside a second bug in the same lines: boxes were sized against the pane rather than the rendered image rect, so letterboxing displaced every box.

error_message: Latin-tuned typography breaks Arabic: tofu glyphs, shattered words, unreadable labels
root_cause: Three separate defects. (1) The bundled IBM Plex Sans has no Arabic glyphs, and FontFamily selects by weight not glyph coverage, so merging faces would not help. (2) The export's letter-spacing breaks the joins between letters in a cursive script. (3) labelCaps is 11sp uppercase, meaningless in a script with no letter case.
fix: Bundle IBM Plex Sans Arabic and BRANCH the family by script; zero letterSpacing for Arabic; grow labelCaps 1sp and drop its tracking; add ~10% lineHeight so ascenders/harakat do not clip.

error_message: Repeated self-inflicted breakage from broad python str.replace on source files
root_cause: Patching Kotlin with str.replace against remembered formatting: Spotless had reformatted the files, so anchors matched partially or matched text that had already been rewritten. Results included a sealed interface spliced into the middle of a data class body and a duplicated @Composable annotation.
fix: For multi-line structural edits, replace by LINE RANGE after grepping the current structure, or rewrite the file. Always re-read after Spotless has run.

error_message: Reminder queue tab labels rendered as a vertical stack of single letters ('F a i l e d'), in both English and Arabic
root_cause: Each tab's 2dp selection indicator used Box(Modifier.fillMaxWidth()) inside the per-tab Column. fillMaxWidth resolves against the INCOMING max constraint, not the sibling label's width, so the first tab's Column claimed the entire Row width and every later tab was measured at ~one character wide.
fix: Bound the per-tab Column with Modifier.width(IntrinsicSize.Max) so fillMaxWidth means 'as wide as this tab's label row'. Added maxLines=1/softWrap=false on the label and horizontalScroll on the strip so a future overflow clips or scrolls instead of shattering.

error_message: Language toggle crammed into the bottom navigation bar as a fourth slot; completely absent on the wide/rail layout
root_cause: App.kt passed the toggle as AnfasBottomNav(trailing = toggle), which stole width from three real destinations and crowded the bar's end edge. AnfasNavRail's footer slot existed but was never passed anything, so on desktop/tablet there was no way to change language at all.
fix: Moved the toggle to an end-aligned row above the Host on compact, and passed footer = toggle to AnfasNavRail on wide. A language switch is not a navigation destination.

error_message: Members empty state: 'SCAN SHEET' wrapped onto two lines while the adjacent 'ADD MEMBER' stayed on one
root_cause: The two action buttons sat in a plain Row, so on a phone they competed for width and whichever was measured second wrapped its label at a different height from its neighbour.
fix: Switched the actions container to FlowRow with vertical spacing, so the buttons stack on a narrow screen and stay inline on a wide one.

error_message: checkAndroidHostTestAarMetadata FAILED: Dependency 'androidx.core:core:1.19.0' requires Android Gradle plugin 9.1.0 or higher / compileSdk 37
root_cause: androidx-core was pinned at 1.19.0 in the catalog but had no Android-compiling consumer, so the incompatibility was latent. :core:ocr became the first consumer (FileProvider) and surfaced it. AGP is capped at 9.0.1 by the installed Android Studio.
fix: Downgraded androidx-core to 1.18.0, the highest release compatible with AGP 9.0.1 / compileSdk 36, and added it to CLAUDE.md's version-ceiling table next to androidx-lifecycle.

error_message: Intake review table showed Start, End and Plan as empty for every row, while still reporting '4 of 4 rows ready for import'
root_cause: The Android recogniser emitted ML Kit Text.Line boxes. ML Kit fuses text on a shared baseline when horizontal gaps are small, so 'Nov 1, 2023 Dec 1, 2023Monthly' arrived as ONE box spanning x 0.63..0.99 across three columns. A box spanning three columns cannot be assigned to any of them, so all three cells came out blank -- and the row still counted as importable.
fix: Emit word-level Text.Element boxes instead of Text.Line, falling back to the line when a model reports no elements. Verified on a real emulator scan: 21 boxes became 51, and all six columns populate.

error_message: With word-level OCR input the parser produced empty dates and plan, and appended 'Nov', 'Dec' and '2023Monthly' to the member's NAME
root_cause: IntakeSheetParser classified each incoming box independently. That works for line-level input ('Nov 1, 2023' parses as a date) but not word-level ('Nov' parses as nothing), so every fragment fell through to the unclaimed bucket and anything with letters was swept into the name cell.
fix: Added a mergeIntoCells stage that groups a row's boxes into cells by horizontal gap before any classification, making the parser independent of recogniser granularity. Calibrated Tuning.minColumnGap from 0.03 to 0.015 against measured ML Kit output (word gaps 0.005-0.009, column gaps 0.017+). Also replaced the name-cell guard with a strict no-digits rule so fused debris like '2023Monthly' can never enter a name. Two regression tests added.

error_message: Intake footer's IMPORT button rendered as a featureless amber vertical sliver on a phone
root_cause: The footer Row used Arrangement.SpaceBetween with an unweighted Text. Unweighted children are measured first at their full intrinsic width, so 'N of N rows ready for import' consumed the row and the button group was measured at whatever remained. Same class of defect as the AnfasTabs indicator bug.
fix: Gave the label Modifier.weight(1f) so the buttons are measured at intrinsic size and the label takes the remainder, plus FlowRow so the label stacks above the actions on a narrow screen.

error_message: Every cell in the intake and members tables truncated to a few characters on a phone ('Omar Ha...', 'Activ e', 'ACTIO NS', 'ID:' with no number)
root_cause: Both tables lay out columns with Modifier.weight, which is correct at the desktop widths the design was drawn at. On a ~360dp phone the same weights divide the width between four to six columns and every cell clips. On the intake review screen that hides the OCR misreads the screen exists to surface; on members it hid the membership number entirely, which looked like import failing to assign one.
fix: Added a shared AnfasTableScroll that keeps a 640dp minimum table width and scrolls horizontally below it, wrapping only the header and rows so an action footer stays fixed. Applied to both tables. A fillHeight flag is required because forcing fillMaxHeight consumed the height the members footer needed and pushed 'Showing N members' off screen.

error_message: iOS: white bands above the status bar and below the home indicator, framing a #141311 app
root_cause: ContentView applied .ignoresSafeArea(.keyboard) only, so SwiftUI inset the Compose view by the top and bottom safe areas and the window's own white background showed through. App.kt already applies its own safe padding, so the insets were being handled twice — once in the wrong layer.
fix: Changed to .ignoresSafeArea() with no arguments so Compose owns every edge and paints the background full-bleed. Also set UIUserInterfaceStyle=Dark in Info.plist so the status bar draws light glyphs and system sheets arrive in dark mode.

error_message: Android: full-screen white flash on every cold start before the dark app appeared
root_cause: The launch window used the wizard's @android:style/Theme.Material.Light.NoActionBar. That theme only paints the starting window, but that window is the first thing shown on every cold start — white, against a #141311 app.
fix: Added Theme.Anfas (parent Theme.Material.NoActionBar) with windowBackground set to the app background and transparent system bars, and pointed the manifest at it. windowLight*Bar entries were dropped: false is already the default and windowLightNavigationBar needs API 27 against minSdk 24, which fails lint.

error_message: Renewal sheet content was cut off in landscape with no way to scroll to it
root_cause: The root Column had only fillMaxWidth(), so its height was wrap-content. Modifier.weight divides a BOUNDED height, so the weighted child fell back to its intrinsic height, verticalScroll measured its content unbounded, and the column grew taller than the window — the scroll never engaged. In portrait the content happened to fit, which is why it looked fine.
fix: Root is fillMaxSize() and the scroll region uses weight(1f) with fill=true, which bounds the viewport and pins the action footer below it. Verified by rotating a Pixel 9 emulator: the sheet scrolls and Confirm/Cancel stay reachable.

error_message: Bottom navigation had unequal tap targets that moved when the language changed
root_cause: Items were laid out with Arrangement.SpaceEvenly over intrinsically-sized children, so each destination's tap target was sized by its own label — 'Reminders' was visibly larger than 'Intake', and every target shifted between English and Arabic. The selected state also filled the whole cell, so it changed shape per label, and there was no minimum touch target.
fix: Rewrote as equal weight(1f) columns with a 56dp minimum height (clears Material's 48dp and Apple's 44pt), an animated pill indicator behind the icon only, 24dp icons, animated colour transitions, ripple clipped to the cell, and maxLines=1 with ellipsis on the label.

error_message: Table column heading rendered as 'ACTIO / NS', taller than the cells beneath it
root_cause: AnfasTableHeaderCell had no line limit, so a heading narrower than its text wrapped and pushed the header row taller than its own columns.
fix: maxLines = 1 with TextOverflow.Ellipsis — a heading that cannot fit should shorten rather than reflow.
